name: C-K Plastics, Inc.
old_description: A leading manufacturer of custom thermoplastic extruded, injection molded and blow molded plastic parts since 1978.
about:
C-K Plastics operates from St. Louis, Missouri, where it was founded in 1978. The company was acquired by Technical Industries in 2011, continuing a legacy of tackling difficult plastic parts that other manufacturers avoid.

The shop produces custom thermoplastic extruded, injection molded, and blow molded parts, running all three processes under one roof. An in-house tool shop controls tooling design and fabrication, while secondary operations include fabrication, assembly, and special packaging. The facility also maintains a quality database for statistical process control and capability studies, though headcount and floor space are not disclosed.

The company serves a broad range of industries, with documented experience in products such as 45-foot-diameter circular curtain enclosures and non-standard blow-molded bottles requiring specialized head tooling. Customers receive engineering assistance and material selection guidance for filled and unfilled engineered resins.

C-K Plastics emphasizes its willingness to take on challenging geometries and smaller runs, a mindset traced to its founding. The 2018 ISO 2001:2015 certification, lean manufacturing practices, and just-in-time delivery programs are cited as mechanisms to reduce lead times and total cost.

name: C.R. International Inc.
old_description: Providing our customers with quality electronic manufacturing services for over 40 years!
about:
C.R. International Inc. (CRI) is a woman-owned small business headquartered in Laurel, Maryland. Founded in 1981, the company began as a small engineering firm supplying communications and data-processing equipment to federal customers, including protocol adapters and specialized radio/telephone interface devices.

Today CRI operates as a full-service electronic manufacturing services (EMS) provider from an 18,000-square-foot, climate-controlled facility. The shop runs two surface-mount technology lines equipped with DEK screen printers and Mycronic pick-and-place machines capable of placing 01005 components through large BGAs, and offers paste printing, conformal coating (acrylic, silicone, epoxy), box-build electro-mechanical assembly, functional testing, first-article inspection, and component verification. Services span prototype development to volume production, supported by AEGIS manufacturing software for work instructions and process control.

CRI serves aerospace and flight programs, defense and military agencies, communications, industrial, medical, and commercial customers, as well as start-ups. Notable references include NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory—where CRI-populated boards supported pyrotechnic activation on a test flight—and Department of Defense prime contractors who rely on the company for tactical electronics.

The company emphasizes partnership and high-reliability manufacturing, maintaining IPC Class III as its standard process, with personnel trained to J-STD-001 and IPC-A-610, including flight-certified soldering and inspection. Certifications include ISO 9001:2015, ITAR registration, CMMC Level 2 C3PAO, and RoHS compliance, reflecting a focus on mission-critical quality and data security.

name: CAMM Metals, Inc.
old_description: At CAMM Metals, our team specializes in MIG and TIG welding techniques. Whether working with steel, stainless steel, or aluminum, our skilled welders ensure precise and durable welds that meet the highest quality standards.
about:
CAMM Metals, Inc. was founded in 1996 by Al Soucie in his household garage in East Windsor, Connecticut. The company, named after his family members Craig, Al, Marge, and Matt, began as a one-man operation with an iron worker and a kerosene heater. By 1997 it moved into a 3,000‑square‑foot building, and today it operates as a second‑generation, family‑owned job shop and manufacturer from a 17,000‑square‑foot facility in the same town.

The shop provides full‑service metal fabrication including laser cutting, laser tube cutting, water jet cutting, welding (MIG and TIG), CNC machining, and 3D printing. It handles materials such as steel, stainless steel, aluminum, copper, plastics, Inconel, and titanium. Production volumes range from small lots to batches of 10,000 pieces, focusing on small‑ to medium‑sized fabrications, weldments, and OEM equipment for industrial customers.

CAMM Metals serves OEMs across New England and New York State, supporting a broad range of industries since 1996. Its ISO 9001‑certified quality system and single‑source capability for cutting, bending, fabricating, and welding make it a go‑to partner for industrial original‑equipment manufacturers.

The company emphasizes a Continuous Improvement mindset, investing profits into new equipment and cloud‑based software to shorten lead times and maintain tight tolerances. Founder Al Soucie retired in 2015, passing leadership to his sons Matt and Craig; Matt continues to drive modernization and on‑time delivery.

name: CED Central Ohio
old_description: We are regarded as one of the top electrical suppliers in the Columbus Ohio region. From Mansfield to Cincinnati and everywhere in-between. With locations in Columbus and Newark we are poised to help you grow your business.
about:
CED Central Ohio operates two locations in Columbus and Newark, serving a broad swath of central Ohio from Mansfield to Cincinnati. The business is part of Consolidated Electrical Distributors (CED), a national network with more than 700 locations across the United States. No founding year or original founders are disclosed on the company's public pages, and ownership beyond the CED affiliation is not specified.

The company functions as a full-line electrical distributor, stocking residential, commercial, and industrial products from brands such as Square D (Schneider Electric), Southwire, Milwaukee Tool, Acuity Brands, Leviton, Sylvania, and Cooper Lighting Solutions. Beyond product sales, it offers asset management solutions, customer project storage, switchgear quotations and project management, design-build services, lighting design and quotations, and a local delivery fleet. The Columbus and Newark branches maintain what the firm describes as the largest inventory in the market for the region.

Primary customers include commercial electrical contractors, residential electrical contractors, multi-family developers, industrial facilities, utilities, and national accounts. Service areas cover more than a dozen Ohio counties, among them Franklin, Licking, Delaware, Fairfield, Madison, Pickaway, Union, Marion, Morrow, Knox, Perry, and Muskingum.

CED Central Ohio emphasizes a policy of service, integrity, and reliability as its driving force. It differentiates itself through local delivery, a deep stock of core product lines, and dedicated project support such as switchgear quotation and lighting design services.

name: CI Sport
old_description: CI Sport holds over 300 collegiate licenses and wants to work with you! We offer the latest styles of garments and unique designs.
about:
Founded in 1990 in Fargo, North Dakota, CI Sport began as a start-up screen-print company conceived by entrepreneurs Randy Thorson and Warren Ackley. The pair, who were involved in the hospitality industry, created the business to outfit bars and restaurants with decorated uniforms, apparel, and souvenirs. From that small beginning, the company grew into a nationally recognized supplier of decorated apparel with three operating divisions: CI Apparel, CI Sport, and CI Tourism.

Today, CI Sport operates a 73,000-square-foot, state-of-the-art facility in southwest Fargo that houses all decoration production, sales, art creation, digitizing, and inventory under one roof—a rarity in the industry. The company’s core decoration processes are embroidery and screen printing, supported by in-house art and digitizing services. CI Sport serves more than 700 college bookstores across 49 states, manages over 25 e-commerce uniform programs, and operates concept shops and T-shirt towers at collegiate and minor-league venues nationwide.

The collegiate division, CI Sport, holds over 300 licenses and supplies college bookstores, arenas, and sporting-goods stores in all 50 states, while also serving as a local license vendor for several NHL and NBA teams and minor-league baseball and hockey fan shops. The corporate division, CI Apparel, provides custom decorated apparel to businesses across virtually every industry, offering access to brands such as Nike, OGIO, and Columbia. The tourism division, CI Tourism, produces custom resort, lake, and cabin apparel with low minimum orders.

CI Sport emphasizes its fully integrated in-house operation, low minimum orders (12 pieces for embroidery reorders and tourism, 36 pieces for screen printing), and fast turnaround times as key differentiators. The company was built on the premise of controlling every step from design to delivery to ensure quality and speed for collegiate, corporate, and tourism customers.

old_description: Nothing beats custom-crafted, in our opinion. Regardless of how you slice it, custom-made takes the cake. Custom-made furniture is frequently less expensive than pre-fab furniture from “big box” stores. CK12 Designs only uses SOLID recycled wood in their custom furniture, never particle wood. Our wood comes from native Oklahoma trees that have died naturally, been cut down by a homeowner, or been rescued from a warehouse demolition. Local Oklahomans are employed at CK12 Designs, which creates handcrafted custom furniture.
about:
CK12 Designs operates from Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, where it produces custom handcrafted furniture. The company's founding year and original owners are not publicly disclosed, but it emphasizes local employment, staffing its workshop with Oklahoma residents. The business centers on creating made-to-order pieces rather than mass-produced inventory.

The shop builds a range of solid-wood furniture including beam consoles, charcuterie boards, coffee tables, live-edge dining tables, entertainment consoles, mantels, and raw reclaimed lumber. Every piece is handcrafted from solid recycled wood sourced exclusively from native Oklahoma trees that have fallen naturally, been removed by property owners, or salvaged from warehouse demolitions. No particle board or composite materials are used.

CK12 Designs serves residential customers and interior designers seeking one-of-a-kind furniture for homes. Its output fits the custom woodworking and high-end home furnishings segments, with no indication of commercial, hospitality, or institutional contracts in the available information.

The company distinguishes itself by its material sourcing—only solid reclaimed Oklahoma hardwoods—and by keeping production local. The emphasis on modern and industrial farmhouse design, combined with a made-to-order model, positions it as a niche maker for clients who want furniture with a documented origin story and no engineered wood.
